## Articles tagged "Roslyn" (5)

- [My Analyzer Shipped Without Checking Its Own Source](https://daily-devops.net/posts/analyzer-dogfooding-roslyn-mef-pitfall/): NetEvolve.Analyzer never checked its own source. Fixing that hit a silent MEF failure and, hours later, a real multi-targeting bug in NE0008.
- [Incremental Source Generators Done Right: Ship It Without Breaking Consumers](https://daily-devops.net/posts/incremental-source-generators-packaging/): Your generator works flawlessly on your machine and breaks in every consuming project. The code is fine — the package is wrong. Part 4: the layout, the dependencies, and the debugging story that survive shipping.
- [Incremental Source Generators Done Right: Prove the Cache Hits](https://daily-devops.net/posts/incremental-source-generators-testing/): Everyone claims their generator is incremental. Until a test asserts the cache actually hits, that claim is folklore. Here is the test, and the anti-patterns it catches.
- [Incremental Source Generators Done Right: Pipeline Patterns That Scale](https://daily-devops.net/posts/incremental-source-generators-pipeline-patterns/): ForAttributeWithMetadataName visits 99% fewer nodes than CreateSyntaxProvider. But the entry point is only half the story — the shape of your pipeline decides whether the IDE stays fast or grinds on every keystroke.
- [Incremental Source Generators Done Right: The Equality Contract](https://daily-devops.net/posts/incremental-source-generators-done-right/): Your incremental source generator rebuilds on every keystroke — because one record property silently broke the equality contract. Part 1 of 4: the mental model, why ImmutableArray betrays you, and the EquatableArray that fixes it.
